orchestrator_output.reformulated_query: Different types and shapes of magnets natural and artificial magnets Class 6 Science
orchestrator_output.text_narration: Magnets are fascinating materials that attract items made of iron, nickel, or cobalt. To understand magnets better, we classify them based on how they are formed and their physical shapes. Magnets are broadly divided into two main categories: natural magnets and artificial magnets. Natural magnets are found directly in nature, like Magnetite or lodestone, but they have weak magnetic power and irregular shapes. Artificial magnets are man-made using pieces of iron or steel, making them much stronger and available in convenient shapes. Artificial magnets are made in different shapes depending on how they are used. A bar magnet is a simple rectangular rod. A horseshoe magnet is shaped like a U to bring both poles closer together. Cylindrical magnets are shaped like rods or pipes, while ball-ended magnets have spherical knobs at both ends. Based on how long they hold their magnetism, artificial magnets are also classified into permanent and temporary magnets. Permanent magnets keep their magnetic property for a long time, like the stickers on your refrigerator door. Temporary magnets lose their magnetism as soon as the external magnetic force is removed, like an iron nail wrapped with wire connected to a battery.
